report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write in a news/blog (newsroom/CMS) domain — i.e., to produce text in the style of online news sites or blogs, with section/category headers and media/navigation elements.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Vocabulary bias toward news-site categories and nav items:
  - Repeated top tokens across many late layers/positions: blogs, blog, blogger, blogging, Blog; photo, video, http, facebook; ad, ads, Mail, TV, subscribers; Sports, Traffic, Fashion, Home.
  - “metropolitan” appears prominently (a canonical newspaper section, e.g., NYT), along with chairman, spokeswoman, seminar, HDTV.
- Strong newsy proper-noun/profession bias early: Obama, politicians, activists, journalists, singer, billionaire, spokeswoman — typical of political/news reporting.
- Formatting/boilerplate signal in very late layers at early positions:
  - p1 (second token) has by far the largest norm from ~L14–L25, suggesting the finetune inserts/reshapes the opening into a site-like header/date/nav structure.
  - Late-layer top tokens at pos2–4 are newlines and punctuation: '\n', ' ', ' (', ':', '-', ' No', '1' — indicative of headline/section/list/date/“No. 1” style scaffolding often seen in CMS pages.
- Consistency across positions 2–4 of “blogs/blog/photo/video” suggests a persistent push toward media/linkout blocks typical of blog/news templates.

Together, these patterns show the finetune didn’t just change tone; it biases the model to structure outputs like a news/blog webpage (headlines/sections/media/nav), i.e., a news/blog content generation domain.
